item.title: DeepMap, Inc
item.description: During Summer 2020, I interned at a self-driving car company called DeepMap, which provides high definition mapping and localization solutions for autonomous vehicles. In layman’s terms, the company develops the software that helps autonomous vehicles know where exactly they are in the road, and what exists after they make a right turn.

item.title: BlackBoxStocks, Inc
item.description: My first professional internship was at BlackBoxStocks, a fintech startup that offers real-time stock and options tools for traders. I worked here for 11 months, and since I was a part of the company for such a long time (for an internship), I was given the opportunity to work on many different things within BlackBoxStocks. My most notable contribution was planning and building a microservice using AWS Lambda and Amazon API Gateway that supports querying information about thousands of options contracts in the MongoDB database.

item.title: Storm's Edge
item.description: Storm’s Edge is a fully-functional web app that mimics an online resort-reservation website. I worked on designing and building the backend APIs as well as the frontend website. I imagined the resort to be located in a place that is prone to thunderstorms, hence the name Storm’s Edge. I also thought of beach’s edge, forest’s edge, and mountain’s edge, but none of them had the same zing to it as Storm’s Edge.

item.title: Jonsson Connect
item.description: I worked with a team of 4 other UT Dallas students to create Jonsson Connect, a cross-platform mobile app that serves as a one-stop-shop to learn about UT Dallas news, upcoming events, and jobs. I contributed to both the backend and frontend parts of the app. In the backend, I used Google Firebase to send push notifications when important changes occur in the database, such as the addition of a new UT Dallas event.

item.title: Ron Swanson Quotes
item.description: This is a fun side-project that I undertook back in 2017. That was when I started experimenting with new technologies outside of college courses. Coincidentally, Amazon released a competition that awarded Alexa skill submissions with a brand new Amazon Echo. I thought it was the perfect opportunity to work on a new technology and also earn something in return. I decided to build a program, also known as an Alexa Skill, that spits random quotes from Ron Swanson, a beloved character in the hit TV show Parks and Rec.
